title: Per-request sequence-length mediation and kernel probing for padding reduction
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce padding and per-token cost for mixed-length requests by mediating sequence-length decisions on a per-request basis during prefill and early decode. Implement a lightweight 'seqlen mediator' that probes available kernel variants and attention modes (dense / block / local / kv-windowed) at request admission, assigns a dynamic micro-batch bucket, and schedules prefill vs decode ordering to preserve latency SLOs while maximizing packing efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: Seqlen mediator deployed behind runtime admission controller and integrated with existing microbatcher
Kernel-probing API implemented with safe fallbacks (no change to existing SLOs on failure)
Automated benchmark harness showing >= 8% average token-cost reduction for mixed-length production-like trace and <= 3% regression in P99 latency
End-to-end telemetry surfaced in runtime dashboard: bucket distribution, kernel choices, token-cost delta, and fallback counts
Canary rollout plan and rollback playbook documented and reviewed by SRE and PM
tasks: Design: define seqlen-mediator interface and decision signals (first N tokens, client metadata, hinted max_length)
Implement: admission-time probe that runs micro-benchmarks against candidate kernel variants (fast path heuristics, cached results across model-version/hw)
Integrate: extend microbatch scheduler to accept external bucket assignment and dynamic pad target per-batch
Telemetry: emit kernel_choice, bucket_id, pad_saved_tokens, probe_latency to observability pipeline
Bench: run synthetic and production-sampled traces, measure token-cost, P50/P95/P99 latencies, GPU utilization
Docs: PRD + API docs + runbook for canary and rollback
Code Review: open PR and incorporate feedback
comments: 2026-02-12 - Asha Patel: Initial triage — mixed traffic with long-tail prompts wastes ~12% token budget on padding for our standard LLM catalog. Proposal: per-request mediation at admission rather than batch-only heuristics.

2026-02-18 - Diego Martinez: Prototype mediator + local kernel probe completed. Probe uses 20-sample microbench for kernel latency estimates; cached per model+hw for 15min. Seeing promising pad reduction in unit tests.
2026-02-22 - Lina Chen (PM): Design review feedback — ensure no P99 regressions for high-priority customers. Add canary gating on p99 and per-route SLA checks.
2026-02-24 - Ravi Gulati (SRE): Security/ops note — probe must be bounded (time & memory) and run at admission only; add circuit-breaker to fall back to default bucket on any probe error.

2026-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Bench results (synthetic workloads): mixed trace (50% short <=64 tokens, 40% medium 65-512, 10% long >512) -> token-cost -9.6% overall, P50 latency -7%, P99 +1.8% (investigating tail contributors). GPU occupancy increased slightly; batching efficiency up.

2026-03-03 - Asha Patel: Follow-up plan — tighten probe cache TTL from 15min -> 5min for high-churn model builds; add adaptive probe sampling under traffic drift. Creating ENG-9142 as dependency for improved seqlen histogram telemetry (referenced below).

2026-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5124 — mediator core + scheduler hook. Pending review from @ravi and @lina. Unit tests and integration tests included.
2026-03-05 - Code review: @ravi requested explicit time-budget enforcement for probes and a metric for 'probe_fall_back_count' — added to tasks. Preparing canary with 5% traffic and p99 SLO gate.
